correctness.rationale: For G=KG(5,2) on 10 two-subsets and P=conv±(e_u-e_v) in the intrinsic nine-dimensional zero-sum space H, the polar is the bounded polytope of real 1-Lipschitz graph potentials. A polar vertex has connected unit-difference edges and hence an integral labeling modulo constants with range ≤2 (graph diameter 2). For the extreme 0/2 classes A,B, graph adjacency excludes disjoint zero/two sets, so A and B are cross-intersecting families. Counting intersecting 2-subsets of [5] shows a=1 implies b≤6, a=2 implies b≤4, and min(a,b)≥3 is impossible. The exact centered norm squared a+b-(a-b)^2/10 is at most 28/5, with equality only for disjoint extreme pair versus its four cross-pairs; the 15 disjoint pair edges and both signs yield exactly 30 facets with support-distance sqrt(5/28). The concrete three-level potentials have a connected tight-edge graph. The sum of 15 outer products has Gram 6I-5A_J+(12/5)J, eigenvalues 1 (4x) and 16 (5x) on H, forcing every maximal ball center to be orthogonal to a spanning family of tight normals: the unique center is 0. All quantifiers, units and ± facets checked. Independent enumeration over all 3^9 spanning-tree assignments, without executing the source script, produced 2613 Lipschitz potentials, 1410 tight-connected polar vertices, 30 maximizers, score numerator 56; independent integer Gram products match 210/-65/60 before dividing by 25.
residual_risks: Facet count 1410 is finite and independently enumerated; no family of Kneser graphs is proved.
Metric is the inherited Euclidean metric of H, not an arbitrary unimodular R^9 projection.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the canonical cubic, diameter-two 10-vertex distance-regular graph. The associated nine-dimensional symmetric edge polytope is canonical under its vertex embedding. Its exact Euclidean inradius, complete 30-facet equality orbit, and unique largest-ball center connect discrete Lipschitz variance and convex contact geometry. Those are intrinsically meaningful data for this fixed graph, rather than renaming a known facet-count table. The norm bound and spanning certificate are substantively more than a tiny unmotivated constant check.
residual_risks: No formula or classification for larger Kneser graphs; numerical facet count is auxiliary.
sources: KG(5,2) intrinsic edge-polytope description and full equality classification in RESULT.md

scientific_limitations: Specific to KG(5,2) and the ambient R^10 Euclidean metric on the zero-sum subspace; no general Kneser-family theorem and no absolute novelty certificate.
